events.text: {npc} arrives at your pavilion on a white crane with a sealed jade slip and the manners of someone paid to be charming. {ct4_house} has watched your rise, and offers {ct4_offer}. The envoy sips your cloud-tea, admires your garden, and waits, politely, for the word.

effects.log: You press your thumb to the slip. The crane is gone by dusk, and the gifts arrive by noon, wrapped in strings finer than silk.
You return the slip with a courteous word. The envoy smiles as one who files a name away.

choices.text: Ask for a season to consider

effects.log: The envoy bows and says the house is patient. Houses are patient about exactly what they plan to collect.

events.text: At the foot of the White Stairs {npc} bows from a polished cloud-barge and proposes, on behalf of {ct4_house}, {ct4_offer}. The terms are written on rose-gold leaf. They are generous, and generous terms from a great house always cost something later.

choices.text: Agree, and raise a cup to it

effects.log: The leaf is sealed over cups of plum tea. You feel the warm weight of a bond settling on your shoulders.
The envoy does not argue. The barge slips back into the mist, and the mist remembers.

choices.text: Say you will answer after the next full moon

effects.log: The envoy accepts this with smiling ease. Nothing was lost, and nothing was settled.

events.text: A courier in the livery of {ct4_house} reaches the quiet isle where you cultivate and delivers {ct4_offer}, with the compliments of the house and the signature of {npc}. Nobody has ever sent you so much so politely. The courier will wait in the garden for your reply.

choices.text: Send back your seal in agreement

effects.log: The courier carries your seal home. By autumn you wear the house colour and are expected at its table.
The courier takes it without comment. A cold wind seems to follow the crane that carries it away.

choices.text: Ask the courier to return in a season

effects.log: The courier sits under your plum tree for an hour, then rises and thanks you for the tea.

events.text: {npc} is back on your terrace, as pleasant as before, and the question of {ct4_offer} from {ct4_house} has not gone away. The tea is poured. The patient smile is unchanged. This time there is no mention of a season.

effects.log: You give your word, and the relief of the envoy is almost as loud as the bell that rings from the house at noon.
You say it once, clearly. The envoy folds the offer away and does not bow quite so low.

events.text: The envoy {npc} returns for your answer. In your absence the offer of {ct4_offer} has grown a little more elaborate, as offers do when a house is anxious. The cloud-tea steams between you. Everything depends on a single syllable.

effects.log: You say it. The envoy exhales and presents a second slip, already prepared.
You say it. The envoy rises, bows precisely as deep as a closed door deserves, and leaves.

events.text: {npc} of {ct4_house} comes through the courtyard of your pavilion, nods to the guards, and does not stop. The offer of {ct4_offer} is going to someone else, one of the lesser cultivators of the outer isles. You are sealed in your realm, and they walk past you like wind past a stone.

choices.text: Watch them go and let it pass

effects.log: You say nothing. The stone gets no wiser, but it does get older.
The wind passes. You reach again for the stillness it disturbed.

events.text: Your realm is closed behind its seals, and {npc} of {ct4_house} knows it. The envoy greets you with the courtesy owed to a statue, and goes on across the cloud-bridge to the pavilion beyond. No offer comes. You cultivate in a silence that someone chose for you.

effects.log: You write the name down. Nothing may come of it, but you do not forget.
It is a small grace, and no one sees it but you.

events.text: The tie with {ct4_house} comes apart in a single morning: a letter, a stopped stipend, a seal withdrawn from your door. They will say it was your choice, and in a way it was. The pavilion feels both lighter and colder, and the cranes seem to look at you differently.

effects.log: You tidy the pavilion and sweep the stair. A freer road opens ahead.
Some ledgers are best kept off paper. You keep this one in your head.

events.text: The last courtesy of {ct4_house} is withdrawn without a word. The cloud-silk stops arriving, the guest-chair at the Jade Court is given away, and the former friends find urgent business elsewhere. What was a tie is now only a story.

effects.log: Strings cut cleanly are lighter than strings loosened. You breathe.

choices.text: Write a short farewell nobody will answer

effects.log: Politeness does not require a reply. You send it anyway.

events.text: A messenger from {ct4_house} stands at your gate with a grey slip: the house has a feud with a rival line, and it is time to repay the tie. You are asked to stand with them and to name a foe of the rival publicly. It is the sort of request that was always inside the gift.

effects.log: You stand with them and name the foe. The gratitude of the house is real and the feud is now partly yours.
You return the slip. The messenger says nothing, and that silence is a verdict.

events.text: The house that gave you its favour asks something back. {ct4_house} wants your name beside theirs at the next council, and wants your voice raised against the line that has crossed them. The messenger is brisk about it, as if debts were weather.

effects.log: You speak at the council. The line they oppose now counts you among its enemies.
You decline. The house does not threaten you, which is how you know the tie is thinner than before.

events.text: Another grey slip from {ct4_house}, third in a series you have been trying not to count. The house names a rival, a feud and a favour owed. It does not ask for your opinion, only your answer.

effects.log: You go through the motions of loyalty. Something in you wonders how much longer it will be enough.
You write one line of regret. It travels farther than you intended.

events.text: Three calls answered, and the messenger of {ct4_house} brings a final slip: the debt is paid in full. The house will honour its word and ask nothing further. You find you are standing taller on your terrace, and also that you will miss the invitations.

effects.log: You thank them. They thank you. Both of you mean it, and both of you keep your distance.

choices.text: Frame the slip and hang it by the gate

effects.log: A slip that says you owe nothing is worth keeping in sight.

events.text: The ledger of {ct4_house} is closed with your name on the right side of it. Three calls answered, no more owed. The messenger presents the receipt with a bow that says the house is not ashamed to be in your debt either.

effects.log: It is a clean ending, and clean endings are rare.

choices.text: Ask for nothing and go in

effects.log: The favour you do not claim is a favour held in reserve.

events.text: {ct4_house} does not leave a rising guest in peace for long. First comes a betrothal to {bh4_kin}, then a vow of fealty written on jade, then a loftier title, all meant to keep the guest near. Each gift is a thread; every thread runs back to one loom.

choices.text: Accept the match and the title

effects.log: You sign. The house is delighted, and you begin to feel the tug of thread under your sleeves.
You decline each gift in order. The house smiles. It does not stop smiling at you for a long time.

events.text: {bh4_kin} comes to your pavilion with a carefully warm welcome. The house would like to honour you: a better chair, an oath of mutual aid, a bond of blood by marriage. It would also like you not to go far. The highest chair a guest can reach is {bh4_cap}, and they remind you of that gently.

choices.text: Take the chair and swear the oath

effects.log: You swear it. The chair is comfortable, and the cushion has a seam you will find later.

choices.text: Stay a guest, and say so

effects.log: You thank them warmly and keep your own seal. It costs you a seat at the table.

events.text: Gifts are the coin of a great line, and {ct4_house} has opened its whole purse to you: a betrothal, a pledge, a grander name. All of it is aimed at tethering a climbing guest. {bh4_kin} waits at your threshold with the bundle held out in both arms.

effects.log: The bindings are comfortable. You wonder how long it takes to stop noticing them.
The refusal is courteous, and the house takes it that way, for now.

events.text: The house has stopped smiling. {ct4_house} lays a charge against you: a forged complaint, a withheld stipend, a whisper at council. A guest too strong to bind must be broken, and the first cut is paper. Soon there will be sharper ones, unless you leave or dig in.

effects.log: You answer each charge in turn and refuse to move. The house will have to do the rest in the open.
You pack in a night and are on the cloud-road by dawn. Better a free fool than a seated target.

events.text: Expulsion papers from {ct4_house}, drafted in a clerk's neat hand, are waiting on your table. An attempt on your cranes has already failed. {bh4_kin} stops greeting you in the corridors. The message is clear: you cannot stay, or you must stay and win.

effects.log: You tear the papers in half and pin the halves to the door. The corridors go quiet.
You leave the Isle with the cranes and a clear conscience. No one follows for the first week.

events.text: Three small insults, one doctored ledger and a poisoned cup of tea: {ct4_house} has moved from persuasion to harm. You can still see the door of the pavilion from where you sit. You can still decide whether you are a guest or a defendant.

choices.text: Hold your place and fight the charge

effects.log: You send a curt letter and call witnesses. The house learns that the guest keeps ledgers too.
You close the door gently on the way out. You will be remembered here as someone who walked.

events.text: A cousin of {ct4_house} sneers at you across the banquet, loudly enough for the whole terrace to hear: a guest, a hired sword, someone who sits where the blood ought to sit. {bh4_kin} makes no move to correct them. The cloud-wine in your cup goes warm.

effects.log: The cousin laughs, then stops laughing. A few heads turn to you thoughtfully.

events.text: A great house spends its gifts like a gardener spends water, and today {ct4_house} has turned the hose on you. An offered match, an oath, a title: all of them meant to keep a rising guest close. {bh4_kin} stands in your doorway holding the lot in both hands.

effects.log: The bindings are comfortable. You wonder how long it takes to stop noticing them.
The refusal is courteous, and the house takes it that way, for now.

events.text: The house has stopped smiling. {ct4_house} lays a charge against you: a forged complaint, a withheld stipend, a whisper at the elders' table. A guest too strong to bind must be broken, and the first cut is paper. Soon there will be sharper ones, unless you leave or dig in.

effects.log: You answer each charge in turn and refuse to move. The house will have to do the rest in the open.
You pack in a night and are on the road by dawn. Better a free fool than a seated target.

events.text: Expulsion papers from {ct4_house}, drafted in a clerk's neat hand, are waiting on your table. An attempt on your horse has already failed. {bh4_kin} stops greeting you in the corridors. The message is clear: you cannot stay, or you must stay and win.

effects.log: You tear the papers in half and nail the halves to the door. The corridors go quiet.
You leave the house with the horse and a clear conscience. No one follows for the first week.

events.text: Three small insults, one doctored ledger and a spoiled cup of tea: {ct4_house} has moved from persuasion to harm. You can still see the door of your lodging from where you sit. You can still decide whether you are a guest or a defendant.

choices.text: Hold your place and fight the charge

effects.log: You send a curt letter and call witnesses. The house learns that the guest keeps ledgers too.
You close the door gently on the way out. You will be remembered here as someone who walked.

events.text: A cousin of {ct4_house} sneers at you across the banquet, loudly enough for the whole hall to hear: a guest, a hired sword, someone who sits where the blood ought to sit. {bh4_kin} makes no move to correct them. The wine in your cup goes warm.

choices.text: Smile, and let the insult fall

effects.log: It falls on the floor between the cushions. Nobody picks it up.

choices.text: Reply with a courteous line that stings

effects.log: The cousin laughs, then stops laughing. A few heads turn to you thoughtfully.

events.text: The blood of {ct4_house} likes to remind outsiders how far they may rise: to {bh4_cap}, and no farther. A young heir says it to you at the banquet with a smile. Everyone knows it is true. Everyone is watching to see whether you will pretend otherwise.

effects.log: You say it is a fair limit for a guest. The hall cannot decide whether you are humble or sly.

choices.text: Raise your cup and say nothing

effects.log: The heir drinks first, because the silence is too heavy to hold.

events.text: Over dinner someone of {ct4_house} calls you, within your own hearing, the best outsider this generation has seen. It is meant as praise. It lands like a seal pressed on a ledger. {bh4_kin} nods approvingly and does not look at you.

choices.text: Take the praise and the sting together

effects.log: You thank them. The word outsider stays on your tongue all evening.

choices.text: Ask politely what an insider would be called

effects.log: The table laughs uncertainly. The question is remembered.
